descriptions.rgb: The head-mounted camera looks steeply downward in a workshop onto the camera wearer's own light-shirted torso and hands, with a concrete floor roughly 1.5 to 1.7 metres below the camera and no other people visible except for a partially out-of-view leg on the far upper-right floor about 1.5 to 2.0 metres away in the fifth frame. Directly in front of the wearer's waist, about 0.4 to 0.6 metres below the camera and within immediate arm's reach, sits a horizontal rectangular stainless-steel panel raised roughly 0.8 metres above the floor, which is touched by both of the wearer's hands. To the left of the wearer and panel (about 0.5 to 0.8 metres away) are vertical metal frames and a small floor-level motor, while to the right on the floor (about 1.3 to 1.6 metres from the camera and 0.4 to 0.6 metres right of the panel, beyond upright arm's reach) lie corded power tools including a yellow-and-black angle grinder and coiled cables. The wearer's torso and arms heavily occlude the floor directly beneath them—leaving only the toes of the wearer's blue footwear briefly visible under the panel's near edge in frame 3—while the forward section of the steel panel and surrounding workshop walls are cut off by the top and side frame boundaries. From frame 1 to frame 2, the camera wearer turns slightly leftward relative to the panel as both hands move closer together near its near corner, then turns back in frames 3 and 4 to face the panel's near edge squarely with the hands spaced about 0.2 to 0.3 metres apart. In frame 5, the camera pitches forward and upward away from the wearer's chest, bringing the middle and far portions of the steel panel (0.5 to 1.0 metres ahead) and a pile of peeled black-and-white protective film on its surface into view within extended arm's reach.
